title: Practice Exam 1
description: A full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam covering all major topics.

questions.question: A speed limit sign shows the:
choices: Maximum legal speed under ideal conditions
Minimum speed you must always drive
questions.explanation: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions. In rain, fog, or heavy traffic you must drive slower, even if it is below the posted limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Speed Limits / Basic Speed Law

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in a residential or business district is:
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in a residential or business district is 25 mph unless a different limit is posted.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speeds

questions.question: When you see an eight-sided red sign, you must:
choices: Slow down and proceed if clear
questions.explanation: An eight-sided (octagonal) red sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signs

questions.question: A yellow diamond-shaped sign generally means:
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to possible hazards or changes ahead, such as curves, intersections, or merging traffic.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Warning Signs

questions.question: At a four-way stop where two cars arrive at exactly the same time, who has the right of way?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Right-of-Way Rules

questions.question: When you want to make a turn, you must signal continuously during the last:
questions.explanation: You must signal continuously during the last 100 feet before turning. On the freeway you should signal at least 5 seconds before changing lanes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Signaling

questions.question: The safest way to check your blind spot before changing lanes is to:
choices: Turn your head and look over your shoulder
Rely only on your side mirror
questions.explanation: Mirrors do not cover blind spots. Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, then turn your head to look over your shoulder for vehicles or cyclists.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Changing Lanes

questions.question: The recommended minimum following distance under good conditions is at least:
questions.explanation: Use the three-second rule: pick a fixed object, and when the vehicle ahead passes it, count three seconds before you reach the same point. Increase the gap in poor conditions.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance / The 3-Second Rule

questions.question: For an adult 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or more. The limit is 0.01% for drivers under 21 and 0.04% for commercial drivers.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol and Drugs

questions.question: If you are under 21, you may not drive with a BAC at or above:
questions.explanation: California has a zero-tolerance law. Drivers under 21 may not drive with a BAC of 0.01% or higher, which can result from even a small amount of alcohol.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Zero Tolerance Law

questions.question: When a school bus ahead of you has its red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must:
choices: Stop until the lights stop flashing
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully
Pass on the left if no children are crossing
questions.explanation: When a school bus flashes red lights, you must stop in both directions and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing. The only exception is on a divided highway when the bus is on the opposite side of a barrier.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Buses and School Zones

questions.question: In a school zone when children are present, the speed limit is usually:
questions.explanation: Near schools the speed limit is typically 25 mph when children are present or as posted; some zones drop to 15 mph. Always slow down and watch for children.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Zones

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights on, you should:
choices: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop
Speed up to get out of the way
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. Never stop in an intersection.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: California's 'Move Over, Slow Down' law requires you to move over a lane or slow down when you approach:
choices: A stopped emergency or maintenance vehicle with flashing lights
A bicyclist riding in the bike lane
questions.explanation: The Move Over law requires drivers to move into another lane when possible, or slow down, when approaching stopped emergency, tow, or Caltrans vehicles displaying flashing lights.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Move Over, Slow Down Law

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian who is:
choices: Crossing at any crosswalk, marked or unmarked
Only when a crossing guard is present
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection or crosswalk, whether it is marked with paint or unmarked.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrians

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist traveling in the same direction, you must give the cyclist at least:
questions.explanation: California's Three Feet for Safety Act requires drivers to allow at least 3 feet of clearance when passing a bicyclist. If you cannot, slow down and pass only when safe.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so that if the car rolls back, the rear of the tire catches the curb. Set the parking brake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: A red painted curb means:
choices: Parking allowed for a limited time
questions.explanation: A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking. White is for loading/unloading passengers, green is limited-time parking, yellow is for loading freight, and blue is for disabled parking.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Colored Curbs

questions.question: To enter a freeway safely, you should:
choices: Use the on-ramp to match the speed of traffic, then merge
Stop at the end of the on-ramp and wait for a gap
Merge slowly well below traffic speed
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to bring your speed up to match freeway traffic, signal, check your blind spot, and merge smoothly into a gap. Stopping on an on-ramp is dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Entering Freeways

questions.question: Two sets of solid double parallel lines on the freeway mark:
choices: The boundary of a carpool (HOV) lane you may not cross
questions.explanation: Double solid parallel lines mark the boundary of a carpool/HOV lane. You may only enter or exit where the lines are broken (dashed).
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Carpool / HOV Lanes

questions.question: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving is:
choices: Illegal; you must use hands-free operation
Legal as long as you are stopped at a red light
Legal on surface streets but not freeways
questions.explanation: It is illegal to hold and use a cell phone while driving. Adults may use it only in hands-free mode. Drivers under 18 may not use a phone at all, even hands-free.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Distracted Driving / Cell Phone Laws

questions.question: Texting while driving is:
choices: Allowed if you type at a stop sign
questions.explanation: Writing, sending, or reading text messages while driving is prohibited for all drivers regardless of age. It is a leading cause of distracted-driving crashes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Texting While Driving

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means:
choices: The light is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely
Speed up to beat the red light
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. Stop if you can do so safely; if you are already in the intersection, continue through.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:
choices: Stop, then proceed when safe (treat as a stop sign)
Slow down and proceed with caution
The signal is broken; do not stop
questions.explanation: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe. A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Flashing Signals

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center of the road means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is not allowed. A broken (dashed) yellow line on your side means you may pass when it is safe to do so.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pavement Markings

questions.question: When you reach a roundabout, you must:
choices: Yield to traffic already in the circle and go counterclockwise
Stop and wait for all traffic to clear
Enter quickly before checking for traffic
questions.explanation: At a roundabout, yield to vehicles already circulating, enter when there is a safe gap, drive counterclockwise, and signal before you exit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Roundabouts

questions.question: When you are merging onto a freeway, the right of way belongs to:
questions.explanation: Vehicles already on the freeway have the right of way. Drivers merging must yield and find a safe gap before entering.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Merging

questions.question: When driving in heavy rain or fog, you should use your:
questions.explanation: In rain, fog, or snow, use low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility. Hazard lights should not be used while driving normally.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving in Bad Weather

questions.question: If you approach a blind intersection with no stop sign or signal, you should not drive faster than:
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection (one where you cannot see at least 100 feet in each direction during the last 100 feet before crossing), the speed limit is 15 mph.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — 15 mph Speed Limits

questions.question: When you park on a level street with no curb, you should:
choices: Turn your wheels so the car would roll off the road if it moved
Turn your wheels toward the center of the road
questions.explanation: On any hill or slope without a curb, turn your wheels so a rolling car would move toward the edge of the road and away from traffic. Always set the parking brake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: A pentagon-shaped (five-sided) sign indicates:
choices: A school zone or school crossing
questions.explanation: A five-sided pentagon sign warns of a school zone or school crossing ahead. Slow down and watch carefully for children.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Warning Signs

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:
choices: The road is wet, you are being tailgated, or visibility is poor
You are driving on a one-way street
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance to 4 seconds or more when conditions are poor: wet or icy roads, fog, heavy traffic, following motorcycles, or when another driver is tailgating you.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance

questions.question: If you are involved in a collision, alcohol in your system can affect penalties because driving impaired:
choices: Slows reaction time and impairs judgment
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment and coordination, and reduces your ability to drive safely even at levels below the legal limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Effects of Alcohol and Drugs

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog at a corner, you must:
choices: Stop and yield; they have the right of way
Proceed because they will wait for you
questions.explanation: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog has the right of way at all times. Stop and allow them to cross safely; do not honk, which can startle them.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrians with Disabilities

questions.question: When changing lanes on a freeway, you should signal at least:
choices: Only if other cars are nearby
questions.explanation: On the freeway, signal at least 5 seconds before changing lanes to give other drivers enough time to see your intention. Always check mirrors and blind spots first.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Changes on Freeways

questions.question: If your traffic signal turns green but a car is still in the intersection, you should:
choices: Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding
Proceed immediately because you have the green
Honk and drive around the car
questions.explanation: A green light means go only if the intersection is clear. You must yield to vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection before proceeding.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights
